speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for clarifying; the combination of rigidity, tremor, and orthostatic hypotension alongside your gait and speech issues strongly suggests a central nervous system disorder. Given the rapid progression and autonomic involvement, have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits or mental status?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Unremarkable. No known chronic diseases. Social history: Occasionally consumes alcohol. Non-smoker. Works as a bank clerk.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple System Atrophy (MSA-C)

The combination of rapidly progressive gait failure, urinary incontinence, rigidity, tremor, and orthostatic hypotension in a 54-year-old male is highly suggestive of Multiple System Atrophy. While the Brain MRI images were requested to rule out other structural causes, the clinical picture strongly points to this parkinsonian syndrome with early autonomic failure. I am ready to finalize this diagnosis based on the current evidence.
